question: As of December 2024, what has been Zillow's (NASDAQ:Z) acquisition strategy over the past 2 years and how does it align with the company's evolving revenue mix?
answer: The company has made several acquisitions of subscription revenue platforms. On December 8, it acquired Follow Up Boss, a CRM for real estate professionals, for $399 million, with up to $100 million in contingent consideration. On September 11, it acquired Spruce, a title and escrow platform, for $19 million. On July 31, the company acquired Aryeo, a software company for real estate photographers, for $35 million. In the post-COVID tight housing market environment, revenue related to Mortgages and Residential (Premier Agent) has declined. The business has acquired various software subscription revenue businesses as it continues to round out its portfolio of home-buying services.

model_answer:
**Short version:** Over the two years to December 2024, Zillow's acquisitions were small, targeted buys of software for real estate professionals. They fit a strategy of becoming an integrated "super app" for the whole housing transaction. They didn't drive the revenue mix, which was shifting mainly because Rentals and Mortgages grew organically.

## Acquisition activity, roughly Dec 2022 – Dec 2024

| Date | Target | What it does | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jul 2023 | Aryeo | Software for real estate photographers | About $35M total: ~$15M cash plus $20M in stock |
| Sep 2023 | Spruce | Tech-enabled title and escrow platform | About $19M cash |
| Dec 2023 | Follow Up Boss | CRM for real estate agents | $399M cash, plus up to $100M contingent over three years |
| Oct 2024 | Virtual Staging AI | AI tool that digitally stages listing photos | Undisclosed |

Sources: Zillow's FY2024 10-K for Aryeo, Spruce and Follow Up Boss, and Crunchbase for Virtual Staging AI.

**Strategy:**
- **Software for agents and the transaction workflow:** Zillow describes the largest deal, Follow Up Boss, as consistent with its strategy to invest in a more integrated software experience for customers. Aryeo, Spruce and Virtual Staging AI extend that into listing media, title and escrow, and AI-generated content.
- **Tuck-in size:** Apart from Follow Up Boss (about $0.5B), the deals were tens of millions of dollars or less. That is far smaller than ShowingTime (about $500M, 2021) and Trulia ($2.5B, 2015).
- **After Zillow Offers:** Zillow wound down its Zillow Offers iBuying business, completing the wind-down in Q3 2022, which cut headcount by about 25%. The 2023–24 deals came after that pullback. They were capital-light software purchases, not balance-sheet-heavy home buying.
- **Management's framing:** In its Q3 2024 shareholder letter, Zillow said it would keep looking to improve its offerings "whether through buying, building, or partnering". It cited Virtual Staging AI and a 3D-tour sharing deal with Realtor.com as examples.

## Revenue mix

Zillow reports four categories: Residential, Rentals, Mortgages and Other. The figures below are my calculations from reported revenue.

| Period | Residential | Rentals | Mortgages | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2022 | ~78% ($1,522M) | ~14% ($274M) | ~6% ($119M) | $1,958M |
| FY2023 | ~75% ($1,452M) | ~18% ($357M) | ~5% ($96M) | $1,945M |
| Q3 2024 | ~70% ($405M) | ~21% ($123M) | ~7% ($39M) | $581M |

Other revenue, mostly ~2%, makes up the rest. The FY2022 and FY2023 figures come from the FY2024 10-K. The Q3 2024 figures come from the Q3 2024 shareholder letter.

- **Residential is still the core, but its share is falling.** Q3 Residential revenue rose 12% year over year. Premier Agent and other agent-facing products sit here, and so does the software Zillow has been buying.
- **Rentals is the fastest-growing large segment.** Q3 Rentals revenue rose 24% year over year, driven mainly by a 38% increase in multifamily revenue.
- **Mortgages is small but growing quickly.** Q3 Mortgages revenue rose 63% to $39M, driven by 80% growth in purchase loan origination volume.
- **Overall growth:** Q3 total revenue was $581M, up 17% from $496M a year earlier.

## How they fit together

1. **Residential:** Follow Up Boss, Aryeo and Virtual Staging AI deepen the agent workflow. That should make Zillow's agent products stickier, which matters because Residential is still about 70% of revenue. I haven't seen Zillow report separate revenue for these acquisitions, so their financial impact isn't broken out.
2. **Mortgages:** Spruce (title and escrow) is the closest acquisition to the growing Mortgages line. It supports the "buy with Zillow end to end" idea, but the dollars were small.
3. **Rentals:** None of the 2023–24 acquisitions targeted Rentals. Rentals growth came from Zillow's own multifamily marketplace.

So the acquisitions support the transaction-software and integration strategy more than they explain the mix shift. This is my interpretation, not Zillow's stated position. FY2024 full-year results came out after December 2024. They show $2,236M of revenue, with Residential at about 71% and Rentals at about 20%, which continues the same trend.
judge_reason: All three acquisitions and the strategy are correct, but the model misses and contradicts the official decline in Mortgages and Residential revenue by calling Mortgages growing.
